validity.recommendation: no action; real, correctly classified, correctly owned FERC-interstate trunk system
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION: real and well-documented. Enable Gas Transmission, LLC (EGT) is a FERC-regulated interstate natural gas transmission and storage system, confirmed independently by (1) Enable Midstream Partners LP's own SEC 10-K filings for FY2016-FY2020 (five consecutive annual reports, all consistent) describing EGT as 'a wholly owned subsidiary of the Partnership that operates a 5,900-mile interstate pipeline... in Oklahoma, Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Missouri and Kansas', and (2) Rextag Corporation's independent 'Gas Informational Postings' dataset (a third-party aggregator of FERC EBB postings, not affiliated with Enable/Energy Transfer), which lists the same system at 5,900 miles / 6.2 Bcf/d / LA-AR-TX-OK-KS. Current operational status as of Jan 2025 is confirmed by a live EGT operational plan document posted on pipelines.energytransfer.com (dated gas day 01/09/25). None of these sources trace to GEM. CLASSIFICATION correct: Fuel=Gas, a genuine long-haul interstate transmission/storage trunk (not gathering/feeder) -- confirmed by the same SEC 10-K language ('interstate transportation and storage business') and by the system's FERC NGA jurisdiction. DUPLICATE check: compared against the full 45-row Texas-operating roster. No overlap -- P0162 (Mississippi River Transmission / 'MRT') is a genuinely separate Enable Midstream subsidiary (different system, serving TX/AR/LA/MO/IL), not the same physical pipe. No relabeling or double-count found. OWNERSHIP: Owner1 'Enable Gas Transmission LLC' 100% is the correct DIRECT legal owner today. SEC filings confirm EGT is 'a wholly owned subsidiary of the Partnership' (Enable Midstream Partners, LP); Energy Transfer LP's own SEC 8-K (filed at the close of its Feb 2021 merger agreement with Enable Midstream Partners, LP) confirms Energy Transfer completed that acquisition in Dec 2021, becoming EGT's ultimate parent -- but EGT itself remains the intact operating/owning entity (still posting tariffs and capacity under its own name via energytransfer.com's EGT informational-postings portal as of Jan 2025). GEM's Owner1 value tracks the direct owning entity, which is unchanged and correctly recorded; the ultimate-parent change (Enable Midstream Partners LP -> Energy Transfer LP, Dec 2021) is context, not a value error. LOCATION: Start=Texas/End=Louisiana is a directional simplification of what is actually a large multi-state network (system also touches Oklahoma, Arkansas, Missouri, Kansas per every source checked) -- plausible and not contradicted (EGT's Anadarko/Arkoma/Ark-La-Tex basin gas moves west Texas/Oklahoma toward Gulf Coast Louisiana markets, and the 10-K discusses EGT infrastructure feeding the Gulf Run Pipeline into Louisiana), but no source gives a precise start/end pair, so I left Location [ref] UNRESOLVED rather than fabricate false precision. Harvested wiki citation pool (6 citations): opened all 6 -- the Q4 2017 Enable investor-presentation PDF (409) and enablemidstream.com/company/operations/projects/ (404) are both dead (site consolidated into energytransfer.com post-acquisition, not a deletion of the pipeline); eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php and eia.gov/maps/layer_info-m.php are generic EIA data-portal pages, live but not EGT-specific; the bit.ly link resolves to abarrelfull (banned, never cited, not used for anything); the fuelfix.com/Houston Chronicle 2013 Enable-formation article was not independently re-verified this pass (peripheral to this pipeline's own specs) but is not needed given the direct SEC/Rextag corroboration above.

validity.recommendation: revise Capacity toward ~6,200 MMcf/d (the last two independently-corroborated figures) or locate a primary source that actually states 6,600 MMcf/d before pasting a ref onto the current value
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's sheet carries Capacity = 6,600.00 MMcf/d (Capacity [ref] currently blank/MISSING_REF). I checked EGT's design/system capacity across every year it was separately disclosed: Enable Midstream Partners LP's own SEC 10-Ks report EGT capacity as 6.5 Bcf/d (FY2016, filed 2017), 6.5 Bcf/d (FY2017), 6.0 Bcf/d (FY2018), 6.3 Bcf/d (FY2019), and 6.2 Bcf/d (FY2020, filed Feb 2021 -- Enable's LAST standalone 10-K; no FY2021 10-K exists because Energy Transfer completed its acquisition in Dec 2021 and Enable stopped filing separately). Rextag's independent third-party FERC-postings aggregation states 6.2 Bcf/d, matching the most recent (FY2020) SEC figure exactly. So the two most recent, mutually-corroborating, independent readings both land on 6,200 MMcf/d -- not 6,600. No source I found (SEC 10-Ks across 5 years, Rextag, EIA pages, the live EGT informational-postings portal) states exactly 6,600 MMcf/d anywhere; it exceeds every self-reported figure in the 2016-2020 window (range 6.0-6.5 Bcf/d). This could reflect an older CenterPoint Energy Gas Transmission-era figure (pre-2013 Enable formation) that I could not locate and verify, a peak/theoretical rather than current operating capacity, or simply a stale/incorrect number. Declining to paste a ref onto the current 6,600 value since none of my sources support it, and declining to silently overwrite it myself per the no-auto-apply rule -- routing to Update.

fills.researcher_notes: 9,495.00 km = 5,900 miles at the standard 1.60934 km/mi conversion (5,900 x 1.60934 = 9,495.11 km, i.e. an exact match to two decimal places). Enable Midstream's own SEC 10-K (FY2020, its last standalone filing) states EGT operates '5,900 miles of interstate pipelines'; Rextag's independent third-party FERC-postings aggregation states the same 5,900 miles. Two independent origins agreeing exactly -> high/independent.

Enable Gas Transmission, LLC is confirmed as the 100% direct owner in Enable Midstream Partners LP's own SEC 10-K ('a wholly owned subsidiary of the Partnership'), and independently confirmed by Rextag's third-party FERC-postings page ('owned by Enable Midstream Partners, LP ... operated by Enable Gas Transmission, LLC'). Note for ResearcherNotes context (not a value change): Energy Transfer LP completed its acquisition of Enable Midstream Partners, LP in Dec 2021 (Energy Transfer's own SEC 8-K), so the ultimate parent above Owner1 is now Energy Transfer LP -- EGT itself remains the intact, unchanged direct owner.

Operating status confirmed current as of Jan 2025 via EGT's own live daily gas-day operational plan (posted on Energy Transfer's FERC-mandated informational-postings site, gas day 01/09/25), independently corroborated by Rextag's third-party listing of EGT among 'active interstate regulated (FERC) gas pipelines'.
Natural gas transportation/storage system, confirmed by the SEC 10-K's own description and independently by Rextag's gas-pipeline listing.

Declining to fill: no source I found states 6,600 MMcf/d. EGT's own SEC 10-Ks give 6.5/6.5/6.0/6.3/6.2 Bcf/d across FY2016-FY2020, and Rextag's independent aggregation gives 6.2 Bcf/d (matching the FY2020 figure exactly). See the paired 'spec' concern in validity[] recommending the sheet be revised toward ~6,200 MMcf/d or that a source actually stating 6,600 be located before citing it.

Declining to fill with a precise ref: EGT is a large multi-state network (SEC 10-K and Rextag both describe it spanning Oklahoma, Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Missouri, and Kansas, feeding the Anadarko/Arkoma/Ark-La-Tex basins toward Gulf Coast Louisiana markets). Texas->Louisiana is a plausible directional simplification consistent with every source checked, but no source states a specific start/end pair, so citing one would overstate precision. See validity[] for detail.

summary: P0161 Enable Gas Transmission: real FERC-interstate trunk, correctly classified/owned/no duplicate; Length/Owner/Status/Fuel refs added (high, independent SEC 10-K + Rextag); Capacity flagged as a spec concern (sheet 6,600 MMcf/d vs. two independent 6,200 MMcf/d readings, both left UNRESOLVED rather than force a ref onto either figure); Location left UNRESOLVED (network simplification, not wrong).
